title: Upcoming roots Symposium to explore advances in contemporary endodontics
html:
Dental Tribune International

Thu. 26. November 2026

share save

Endodontics plays a central role in dentistry, supporting the long-term preservation of natural dentition. For dental professionals seeking to stay abreast of advances in endodontic materials, technologies and treatment strategies, the upcoming roots Symposium 2026 will offer evidence-based insights and practical clinical guidance. Hosted by Dental Tribune International on its DT Study Club online education platform, the free event will take place on 4 December.

In the opening session, Dr Renaud Giess will examine the influence of endodontic motor kinematics on the mechanical performance of nickel–titanium instruments. His lecture will address how different motion patterns affect torque generation and instrument fatigue, highlighting the implications for clinical decision-making and the limitations of the available scientific evidence.

Dr Harpreet Singh will focus on the scientific principles underlying bioceramic materials, particularly their physicochemical and biological properties. Drawing on published research, his own experimental investigations and clinical cases, he will discuss the evidence supporting their use in root canal obturation and vital pulp therapy.

The importance of tailoring treatment to individual anatomical conditions will be the subject of a lecture by Dr Sławomir Gabryś. Using three clinical cases involving distinct anatomical challenges, he will illustrate strategies for instrument selection, canal preparation and obturation, as well as measures to minimise the risk of procedural errors.

Specialty symposia to continue in 2027

The roots Symposium 2026 forms part of an ongoing series of online specialty symposia, which has attracted several thousand dental professionals worldwide since its launch in 2025. The initiative aims to make continuing education internationally accessible and facilitate the integration of scientific findings and technological developments into everyday dental practice.

Seven further symposia have already been scheduled for next year, covering digital dentistry and artificial intelligence, CAD/CAM, 3D printing, implantology, cosmetic dentistry and facial aesthetics, aligner orthodontics and endodontics.

Participants in the roots Symposium 2026 can earn up to five continuing education credits by completing the corresponding educational activities and quizzes. The full programme and free registration are available on the DT Study Club website.
